main.title: Call of Duty: WWII
main.subtitle: Back to the Western Front
main.summary: Call of Duty: WWII is a 2017 first-person shooter game developed by Sledgehammer Games and published by Activision. It was released worldwide on November 3, 2017, for PlayStation 4, Windows and Xbox One. It is the fourteenth main installment in the Call of Duty series and the first title in the series to be set primarily during World War II since Call of Duty: World at War in 2008.

cards.heading: Back to the Second World War
cards.text: Call of Duty: WWII is a 2017 first-person shooter game developed by Sledgehammer Games and published by Activision. It was released worldwide on November 3, 2017, for PlayStation 4, Windows and Xbox One. It is the fourteenth main installment in the Call of Duty series and the first title in the series to be set primarily during World War II since Call of Duty: World at War in 2008.

cards.heading: A squad between campaign and multiplayer
cards.text: The game's campaign is set in the European theatre and is centered around a squad in the 1st Infantry Division following their battles on the Western Front beginning with Operation Overlord (D-Day) and following the advance into Germany. The player controls Ronald "Red" Daniels, who has squadmates who can supply the player with extra ammunition, health, or grenades as well as a targeted grenade and target spotting; none of these are automatically replenished in the campaign. The multiplayer mode features map locations not seen in the campaign. The mode also features the new Divisions system, replacing the create-a-class system that previous games in the series used. A social hub, named Headquarters, was also implemented into the game, allowing for players to interact with each other.

cards.heading: The decision to return
cards.text: Sledgehammer Games were interested in bringing the series back to World War II after developing their previous title, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare (2014), which featured advanced movements and futuristic warfare technology. Studio head Michael Condrey stated that he was unsure if a World War II game would feel right after creating a futuristic title like Advanced Warfare, but the developers ultimately decided to create a game in this time period. They also chose to include atrocities and Nazi concentration camps in the campaign mode to deliver an authentic war story.

cards.heading: Reception and commercial success
cards.text: Upon release, the game received generally positive reviews from critics. Praise was given towards its story, the changes to combat, multiplayer modes, and visuals. However, it was criticized for the single-player's lack of innovation and similarity to past games set in the same era. Retrospective reviews have been mixed. The game was a commercial success, generating $500 million of revenue within just three days of its release. It became the highest-grossing console game of 2017 in North America, and generated over $1 billion in worldwide revenue by the end of the year.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2017
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2017 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon
main.subtitle: Alola takes another path
main.summary: Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon are Game Freak's expanded Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventures returning to the island region of Alola. They revisit Sun and Moon with an alternate storyline centred on Necrozma, new characters and additional activities. The player's journey through the region retains its familiar battles, exploration and growing team, while the Ultra Recon Squad and new forms of Legendary Pokémon change the larger mystery. These were the final mainline Pokémon releases for the 3DS family, giving the portable generation one more substantial version of its distinctive tropical setting.

cards.heading: Alola takes another path
cards.text: Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon are Game Freak's expanded Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventures returning to the island region of Alola. They revisit Sun and Moon with an alternate storyline centred on Necrozma, new characters and additional activities. The player's journey through the region retains its familiar battles, exploration and growing team, while the Ultra Recon Squad and new forms of Legendary Pokémon change the larger mystery. These were the final mainline Pokémon releases for the 3DS family, giving the portable generation one more substantial version of its distinctive tropical setting.

cards.heading: Beyond the next island
cards.text: Ultra Warp Ride allows travel through Ultra Wormholes into other destinations, including the worlds associated with Ultra Beasts. Mantine Surf offers another way to move between the islands' seas, connecting a new activity to the region's geography. Totem Stickers provide a collectible route toward unusually large Pokémon, while the Alola Photo Club lets a trainer pose with a companion. These additions broaden what can occupy the journey between major encounters. The familiar adventure gains more reasons to move around its islands and to spend time with the team already assembled.

cards.heading: Old rivals meet after the journey
cards.text: The post-game Team Rainbow Rocket story brings together leaders from earlier antagonistic teams, extending the adventure's connection to Pokémon history. Necrozma's new forms also make its relationship with Solgaleo or Lunala central to the visual identity of the two versions. The expanded structure mixes that retrospective interest with further discoveries in Ultra Space. Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon give returning players another account of Alola, using new routes and encounters to keep a recognisable place active after the broad outline of its first journey has become familiar.

main.title: Star Wars Battlefront II
main.subtitle: Three eras, a new Imperial perspective
main.summary: Star Wars Battlefront II is DICE?s 2017 shooter spanning three film eras, with a campaign following Imperial commander Iden Versio.

cards.heading: Iden Versio’s story
cards.text: Star Wars Battlefront II is a 2017 shooter developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts. Its battles draw on the original, prequel and sequel film trilogies. Motive Studios created the campaign, which follows Imperial Inferno Squad commander Iden Versio between Return of the Jedi and The Force Awakens. Criterion Games developed the starfighter combat.

cards.heading: Progression and controversy
cards.text: Prior to launch, the game came under widespread criticism when players discovered that the game's loot boxes were tied to progression, which could give players substantial gameplay advantages if purchased with real money. EA initially defended the lootboxes, leading to further controversy, though the company eventually disabled microtransactions in the game. Following launch, a new progression system was introduced.

cards.heading: From release to content updates
cards.text: The game was released worldwide on November 17, 2017, for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Microsoft Windows. Battlefront II received mixed reviews from critics, with praise for the multiplayer, gameplay, balancing, visuals, and variety, but criticism for its single-player modes, campaign, microtransactions, and progression system. After its release, the game received numerous content additions through free updates, some of them tie-ins to recently-released content, in an attempt to repair its reputation after launch, which brought in a large number of new players. Regular content updates ended on April 29, 2020 with The Battle on Scarif; DICE described its vision for the game as complete, while servers, events and game support continued. A Celebration Edition of the game, which includes in-game-purchasable customization content up to the December 2019 Rise of Skywalker update, but not subsequently released items, was released on December 5, 2019.
